messages.content: In plain English, what does idempotent mean in programming? Keep it to two short paragraphs.

In programming, idempotent means that performing an action multiple times has the same effect as performing it once. No matter how many times you repeat the operation, the end result doesn't change after the first execution. Think of it like setting a thermostat to 72Â°F â whether you press the button once or ten times, the temperature stays at 72Â°F.

This concept is especially important in APIs and database operations. For example, an HTTP GET request is idempotent because fetching the same page repeatedly returns the same data without side effects. In contrast, something like "add $10 to my balance" is not idempotent â doing it twice gives you $20 extra, not $10. Idempotency helps systems handle retries safely without causing unintended duplicate effects.
